stem.en: Engineers are building a robot arm. Its middle joint must bend and straighten in one direction only, like a door, with no sideways movement and no twisting. Which type of joint should they copy?

text.en: A ball and socket joint, which allows the widest range of movement.

feedback.en: No. A ball and socket joint allows sideways and circular movement, which is exactly what the robot arm must not do.

text.en: A pivot joint, which lets one part turn from side to side on another.

feedback.en: No. A pivot joint turns from side to side. The arm would twist instead of bending.

text.en: A hinge joint, which allows movement in one direction only.

feedback.en: Yes. A hinge joint, like the elbow, bends and straightens in one direction only, like a door.

text.en: A fixed joint, which allows no movement at all and so stops all twisting.

feedback.en: No. A fixed joint would stop the twisting, but it would also stop the bending the arm needs.

explanation.en: The robot arm needs two things: bending in one direction, and no movement in any other direction. A hinge joint does exactly this, which is why the elbow and the knee bend like a door. A ball and socket joint allows too much movement, a pivot joint turns instead of bending, and a fixed joint does not move at all.

hints.en: The joint must allow one thing and stop everything else. What must it allow?
Which joint in your arm bends like a door?
